title: The Prophet of Light
tagline: A visionary paints his gospel across three continents in color and light.

scenes.text: Persia, 240 CE. A young man has a vision: an angel commands him to announce a new religion — one that will combine the teachings of Zoroaster, Buddha, and Jesus into one universal truth. Mani obeys.

scenes.speaker: Mani
scenes.text: God of Light did not create darkness. Evil is not God's failure — it is a separate, opposing force. The universe is a battlefield between light and darkness, and every human soul is the ground on which that battle is fought.

challenge.instruction: Mani taught his vision in pictures as well as words. Piece together the page of his Picture Book that shows the battle of Light and Darkness.
challenge.fact: Mani (216–274 CE) founded Manichaeism, a dualistic religion blending Zoroastrian light-and-darkness cosmology, Christian ethics, and Buddhist concepts of spiritual purification. At its height, Manichaeism spread from the Roman Empire to Tang Dynasty China — one of history's most geographically expansive faiths.

scenes.text: Mani traveled from Persia to India to Central Asia, winning converts among merchants, princes, and scholars. His church spread across the known world within his own lifetime — from Rome to China.

scenes.speaker: Mani
scenes.text: I am not founding a new religion separate from the others. I am giving the world the complete scripture — the final synthesis. After me, no new prophet is needed. I bring what the others began.

challenge.instruction: From Persia, Mani's letters go out to every congregation on the royal roads. Plan a round that carries them to every town and back to the prophet.
challenge.fact: Mani wrote his scriptures himself, in a script adapted from Syriac, so that his teaching would not be corrupted after his death as he believed the teachings of Zoroaster, the Buddha and Jesus had been.

scenes.text: The Zoroastrian high priest Kartir convinced the Persian king to turn against Mani. Imprisoned and executed in 274 CE, Mani died in chains. His followers called it 'The Crucifixion.' His church survived for a thousand years after him.

challenge.instruction: Kartir has turned the king against him, and Mani lies in chains. Read his last message to the church as his disciples signal it, letter by letter.
challenge.fact: Mani's death in 274 CE echoed the martyrdom narratives of the very religions he synthesized. His followers spread his teachings across the Silk Road for centuries — Manichaean texts were still being copied in China in the 13th century.

challenge.instruction: Mani taught through parables — stories of light trapped in darkness. Complete his parable of the soul's journey from matter back to the realm of pure light.
challenge.fact: Mani believed the material world was a prison of darkness and that human souls were fragments of divine light awaiting liberation. His parables, hymns, and paintings were all instruments of the same message: light will eventually triumph over darkness.

challenge.instruction: A thousand years on, Mani's books lay buried in the sand of the Silk Road. Dig the ruins of Kocho and bring them back to the light.
challenge.fact: Mani composed hymnbooks in multiple languages, including Middle Persian, Parthian, and Syriac. The Coptic Manichaean Psalm-Book, discovered in Egypt in 1930, preserves hundreds of hymns that reveal a sophisticated musical tradition within his church.

scenes.speaker: Mani
scenes.text: Hua Mulan and Mahavira hold Damascus together, and a follower stands with them. One card alone will not move them. Bring Anaxagoras with me, add both followers, and strike twice.

challenge.instruction: Fight lesson 2 · Strength in Numbers. Over two turns stack Mani, Anaxagoras and both followers at Damascus, then win two attacks against the rival side.
challenge.fact: An attack compares whole sides at a location, not single cards. Two Great People and two followers in the same stat outweigh a rival who arrived first, and each win sends one rival card back to its owner's hand.
